label: PowerSync (self-hosted Open Edition)
licence: Service: FSL-1.1-ALv2 (source-available, converts to Apache-2.0 two years after each release). Client SDKs: Apache-2.0 / MIT.

pgCapture.note: Logical replication from Postgres (also MongoDB, MySQL, SQL Server).

partialSync.note: Sync rules define buckets parameterised from JWT claims; expressive, but a second query language beside SQL and our FilterTree.

offlineWrites.note: Best offline story of the four: durable local SQLite, upload queue, write checkpoints ordering server acknowledgement against the sync stream.

permissions.note: Postgres RLS is not part of the path; authorisation lives in the sync-rules YAML, a third policy language we would have to keep in step with PAP-34 RLS and PAP-59 can().

bundle.note: wa-sqlite WASM is roughly a third of PGlite; OPFS is the default on Chrome and Firefox, and Safari no longer needs COOP/COEP headers.

targets.note: Strongest Tauri story: a native Tauri SDK backed by Rust SQLite exists precisely because IndexedDB/OPFS reset on every Tauri app update. It is still alpha.

selfHostLicence.note: Self-hosts in Docker (Open Edition, free), but the service is source-available under FSL, not OSI open source, until the two-year Apache conversion. Needs a recorded re-open trigger under PAP-212.

maturity.note: Mature and shipping fast (service 1.23.3 in July 2026, 1.26.1 by September 2026); multiple production client SDKs.

ergonomics.note: Good TypeScript SDK with Drizzle and Kysely wrappers, but the local store is SQLite: our Postgres schema (uuidv7, citext, jsonb, generated columns) has to be projected and queries written twice.

exit.note: Sync rules and the SQLite local schema are PowerSync-shaped; the backend connector is small. Moderate.
